name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,775

entries.clue: Drugs ultimately wanton king rolled in joint (4)

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of 'wanton'
something rolled over is turned end to end, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: E = ecstasy; two of them make Drugs

annotation.surface: A drug-addled monarch reels about in a smoky den with a joint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint' plays on the cannabis cigarette of the drug surface; it is really a body joint. EENK read backwards gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the hinge between thigh and shin is one of the body's joints.

entries.clue: Congress introducing new law unamended? (6)

indicators.note: Congress takes the next letter into itself

blocks.note: an act of Parliament is a law

annotation.surface: A question about whether a legislature can bring in a new law and leave it unchanged.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the US legislature, which suits law; here it means sexual congress, the crossword IT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something left whole, with nothing altered or taken away.

entries.clue: One pinched by criminal? (4)

indicators.note: to be pinched is to be squeezed between, so the criminal holds the one inside him

blocks.note: a con = a convict, a criminal

annotation.surface: Someone wonders what a crook might steal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a coin is just the sort of thing a thief pinches, in the sense of steals. Wordplay has I squeezed inside CON.
annotation.definitionFit: The &lit reads straight because pinched also means stolen, and loose change is the classic haul of a petty thief.

entries.clue: Go out with anorak and jumper (8)

indicators.note: out as in wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Advice on what to wear outdoors: a waterproof coat and a sweater.
annotation.walkthrough: An anorak is a hooded waterproof coat and a jumper is a sweater in British English, so the surface is a clothing list; the jumper here is a leaper.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the Australian marsupial gets about by leaping, so it is a jumper in the literal sense, not the sweater.

entries.clue: Everybody hates me for demolishing still (3,3,4)

indicators.note: what is demolished is broken up, so the letters of 'hates me' are knocked down and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A wrecker complains that the whole town resents him for knocking down a building that still stands.
annotation.walkthrough: Still looks like part of the demolition scene; it is the adverb meaning nevertheless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the adverb sense: both mean nevertheless, in spite of that.

entries.clue: Hit single by popular tenor and Love (3,4)

blocks.note: in cricket a single is one run
T = tenor, as in SATB choir parts
love = nil = O, as in tennis

annotation.surface: A chart-topping record by a well-liked tenor with a band called Love.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hit single' reads as one pop phrase, but it splits: Hit is the definition and single is the cricket run.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal-verb synonym: colliding with something, as a car does a lamppost, is striking it.

entries.clue: You have to say check time the PM’s in power? (5)

indicators.note: tells you to speak the word, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a rein is the strap that checks a horse; the word is wanted only for its sound

annotation.surface: A political commentator wondering whether it is time to curb the Prime Minister's power.
annotation.walkthrough: REIN is said exactly like REIGN. The question mark flags a stretched definition: a PM holds office rather than rules as a monarch does.
annotation.definitionFit: Extended sense: the word for a monarch's period on the throne is borrowed for any long spell in charge.

entries.clue: Titan unfortunately shrouds side of Tethys (5)

indicators.note: a shroud wraps round something, so ALAS goes around the letter
takes one edge letter of Tethys, here the first

annotation.surface: An astronomical scene: Saturn's moon Titan sadly blocks the view of its neighbour moon Tethys.
annotation.walkthrough: Titan and Tethys are both moons of Saturn, which makes the surface astronomy; they are also both Titans of Greek myth, and Atlas is the one wanted.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in Greek myth he is one of the Titans, condemned to hold up the sky.

entries.clue: Perhaps measure of gin and it in the end is top (7)

indicators.note: takes only the final letter of 'it'

blocks.note: a single is one measure of spirits; Perhaps marks it as one example

annotation.surface: Someone muses that a gin and It (gin and Italian vermouth) is ultimately the best drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Gin and It is a classic cocktail, which disguises the split; top is a noun, the garment.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a sleeveless vest is one kind of top, the garment.

entries.clue: Seductive singer stripping off northern father (4)

indicators.note: a stripper sheds clothes, and the singer's word sheds a letter

blocks.note: the Sirens lured sailors with song

annotation.surface: A temptress entertainer undresses in front of a man from the north with children.
annotation.walkthrough: Stripping off fits the seductive singer in the surface; here it removes the N from SIREN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as noun or verb: the male parent, especially of a horse, or to beget.

entries.clue: Denying oneself gin? Bang tea on! (10)

indicators.note: slang for tipsy or high, so the letters before it are in no fit state and get rearranged

annotation.surface: A teetotaller refuses the gin and demands the kettle be put on instead.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface splits the fodder with a question mark so gin seems to go with the self-denial; all three words are mixed together.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: renouncing or going without something you want.

entries.clue: Judge about to imprison German horseman (6)

indicators.note: about as in turned about, facing the other way, so the word for judge is read backwards
a prison holds someone inside, so the reversed word locks G within it

annotation.surface: A magistrate is about to jail a German rider.
annotation.walkthrough: Judge looks like a noun, the person on the bench; it is the verb to reckon. KNIHT then takes G into its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Historical sense: the medieval title began as a mounted soldier, a warrior on horseback.

entries.clue: Biscuit and red juice 11 tucks into (10)

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, so the letter enters SAP

blocks.note: 11 is KNIGHT, and N = knight in chess notation

annotation.surface: A snack of a biscuit and tomato juice that someone is eating eagerly.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to KNIGHT, but only its chess abbreviation N is used, so tucks into the sap.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a crisp, spiced cookie is one kind of biscuit, the British word for cookie.

entries.clue: Motorway and a river ring a foreign resort (8)

blocks.note: British motorways are M roads (M1, M25)
to ring = to give a bell, i.e. phone

annotation.surface: Travel directions: take the motorway, follow a river and phone ahead to a resort abroad.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is 'foreign resort', with its a used by the wordplay. Marbella is a resort on Spain's Costa del Sol.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a Costa del Sol town is a resort abroad from the British setter's point of view.

entries.clue: My boss, being sat on by geezer, is shocked! (5)

blocks.note: a geezer is British slang for a man
the setter's boss is the editor, ED

annotation.surface: An employee is appalled to see their boss sat on by some bloke.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, sat on by puts MAN above ED. Shocked here means having a shock, a thick mass, of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: Punning sense: a shock is a thick mass of hair, so shocked is read as having one, like a lion.

entries.clue: American bum kidnaps Latin family (4)

indicators.note: a kidnapper holds the victim inside, so CAN goes round L

blocks.note: can is US slang for buttocks

annotation.surface: A US tramp abducts a Hispanic family.
annotation.walkthrough: Bum looks like the American word for a tramp, but it is the British sense, bottom, and the American synonym for that is CAN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a group of related households, as in a Scottish kinship group.

entries.clue: Fast to save island nurse, showing mercy (7)

indicators.note: the fast keeps the letters safe inside it

blocks.note: Lent is the Christian fast before Easter

annotation.surface: A rescuer rushes to save an island nurse, proving compassionate.
annotation.walkthrough: Fast reads as quick in the rescue scene; it is the noun, a period of fasting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adjective phrase for someone inclined to go easy on others.

entries.clue: Daughter gets shot then eats hot dog (5)

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside, so D and GO together swallow IN

blocks.note: a shot = a go, an attempt

annotation.surface: A girl has a jab and then grabs a frankfurter.
annotation.walkthrough: Hot dog looks like one snack, but hot belongs to the wordplay and dog alone is the definition. The container wraps the daughter and her shot together, not the shot alone.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Australia's wild canine is one kind of dog.

entries.clue: Set off at ten with doe in need of treatment (8)

indicators.note: letters that need treating are to be worked on and put into a new order

annotation.surface: Someone leaves at ten o'clock with an injured deer that needs a vet.
annotation.walkthrough: Set off reads as depart in the travel surface; it means to explode something.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the explosives sense: what you do to a bomb, not to a journey.

entries.clue: Opponent in top shape cut by heartless nut (4)

indicators.note: A1 is split open and the other letters go in the cut
the middle of nut is removed

blocks.note: A1 = first-rate, in top shape; the 1 is written I
NUT without its middle letter U

annotation.surface: An opponent who is fighting fit is stopped by a mindless lunatic.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 is written with the numeral 1 read as the letter I, a common crossword swap. An anti is someone against something.
annotation.definitionFit: The prefix meaning against also stands alone as a noun for a person against something.

entries.clue: Refurbish diner vet turned upside down (8)

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes something, so the letters are rebuilt

annotation.surface: An instruction to renovate a restaurant that an animal doctor has trashed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end, and it doubles as the scene: a diner turned upside down needs refurbishing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, a past participle matching the participle phrase in the clue.

entries.clue: Chaps on bit of Benzedrine about to get port (6)

blocks.note: chaps = men; on puts them after B and RE

annotation.surface: Some blokes on amphetamines are about to go and fetch some fortified wine.
annotation.walkthrough: Benzedrine is an amphetamine brand, and port the fortified wine, which keeps the surface in a druggy pub; port is the harbour city. In an across clue, on places MEN after.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the German city on the River Weser is a major harbour.

entries.clue: Bust leader of assassins in French port (6)

indicators.note: takes the first letter of assassins
puts that letter inside the port

blocks.note: Brest is a naval port in Brittany

annotation.surface: A police raid on a gang of killers in a French harbour town.
annotation.walkthrough: Bust looks like the verb, a police raid; it is the noun, a woman's chest.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name the chest or bosom.

entries.clue: Had board elected all the eccentric nobs at summit? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: EATEN is a participle, as in having had board, i.e. having been fed

indicators.note: the nobs, the heads, are at the top of each word in a down clue

blocks.note: first letters of elected, all, the, eccentric, nobs

annotation.surface: A question whether the company board voted in a gang of odd toffs at the top.
annotation.walkthrough: Nobs is British slang for posh people, and also for heads, which is its job here. Board means meals, as in bed and board.
annotation.definitionFit: Board is an old word for meals, so to have had board is to have had your food, taken as the past participle.

entries.clue: Fairly-priced ales on bar drunk by English (10)

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, and so do the letters of ales on bar

annotation.surface: Cheap beer at the pub counter, knocked back by the English.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's drinkers are the English; here English just adds E after the rearranged letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the pricing sense: not expensive, fair to the buyer.

entries.clue: Party drug makes head go blue initially (4)

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, is replaced
takes the first letter of blue

blocks.note: first letter of blue, which takes H's place

annotation.surface: A narcotic at a party turns someone's head blue.
annotation.walkthrough: Head reads as a person's head in the surface; it is the first letter of HASH.
annotation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: the slang word for a lively celebration.

entries.clue: Topless harlots in etching and painting? (4)

indicators.note: removes the top, the first letter

annotation.surface: A saucy nude portrait of prostitutes in art.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: etching and painting are two of the arts.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: the two are instances of creative disciplines.

entries.clue: A large one gets foremost of topers settled (4)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A big drink is served first to the heavy drinkers and calms them down.
annotation.walkthrough: A large one is British pub talk for a big measure of spirits, and topers are drunkards; the words are used separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary past tense of alight, to come down and land, as a bird on a branch.

entries.clue: Breakfast? Little drink with a drop of sherry in it! (5)

indicators.note: the letters go inside the little drink
a drop is a tiny amount, the first letter

blocks.note: a tot is a small drink

annotation.surface: Someone's idea of breakfast is a small glass with a dash of sherry in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks Breakfast as an example: toast is one breakfast item.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: browned bread is a morning staple.

entries.clue: Fixed idea old boy expressed in boozy binge (7)

indicators.note: to express is to press out, as juice from fruit, so OB is squeezed out

blocks.note: an obsession is a fixed idea
OB = old boy, a former pupil; removed

annotation.surface: A former schoolmate voices his pet theory during a drinking spree.
annotation.walkthrough: Expressed looks like spoken in the surface; it means squeezed out.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: the word for a meeting or sitting also means a long bout of heavy drinking.
